correctness.rationale: The expected range is exactly \(\sum_j[1-P_j^N-(1-P_j)^N]d_j\). The centered parent is \(\sum_jd_jH_j\), so the \(L^2\) triangle inequality gives the lower constant; with at least two positive gaps the nested centered indicators are not positive scalar multiples, making the lower inequality strict, and one dominant gap gives sharpness. The extreme-order mass identities give the exact covariance with the cellwise secant slopes of \(u^N+(1-u)^N\); strict convexity makes those slopes strictly increasing, so Cauchy--Schwarz has an admissible unique affine equality support. Connectedness gives the full interval. Fresh exact-rational replay checked 2500 independent profiles/supports and all displayed inequalities and score ordering.
